claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons have substantial nanostructural disorder.
As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons contain significant residual stress.
As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons have a high defect density.
Short, moderate-temperature RTA induces structural relaxation in FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons.
Post-deposition RTA promotes ordering in the alloy film.
RTA reduces internal stress and defect density, particularly at grain boundaries, in FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons.
Reduced stress, reduced defect density, and improved short-range order decrease domain-wall pinning.
Decreased domain-wall pinning enables smoother domain switching and a more reversible low-field cyclic magnetic response.
RTA-treated samples will have narrower magnetic hysteresis loops than otherwise identical as-deposited samples.
RTA-treated samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric temperature change per unit applied-field change than as-deposited samples.
The as-deposited baseline has significant hysteresis and a muted magnetocaloric response because of disorder and high defect density.
Any RTA benefit is limited to cycle rates that do not exceed the film-substrate system's heat-transfer capability.
Extreme temperatures or high field-sweep rates may mask the predicted RTA improvement.
RTA can substantially alter the magnetic properties of an HEA thin film.
